primitives.name: ForcePose Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: We present ForcePose, a novel deep learning framework that estimates applied forces by combining human pose estimation with object detection.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'force magnitude in Newtons (N)', 'θ': 'force direction in degrees', 'P': 'human pose landmarks', 'O': 'object detection bounding boxes'}
primitives.assumptions: Human-object interactions are captured in video; pose and object data are temporally aligned; force estimation is deterministic within a trained model's domain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when object occlusion exceeds 50% or pose estimation confidence drops below 0.5.

layer2.mapping: ForcePose's spatiotemporal feature maps are isomorphic to GSI's Bayesian belief states over force magnitude and direction.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error in force magnitude (5.83 N) and direction (7.4°)

primitives.name: MediaPipe Pose Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our approach uses MediaPipe for skeletal tracking and SSD MobileNet for object recognition to create a unified representation of humanobject interaction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_i': 'i-th pose landmark in 2D space', 'T': 'temporal sequence of poses', 'C': 'confidence score of pose estimation'}
primitives.assumptions: Skeletal joints are detectable in 2D image space; temporal consistency is maintained via smoothing filters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pose estimation fails when joint visibility drops below 0.3 or occlusion exceeds 70%.

layer2.mapping: MediaPipe's pose kernel is embedded into GSE's kinematic state vector for motion planning.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal smoothing via Savitzky-Golay filter reduces pose jitter

primitives.name: SSD MobileNet Object Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our approach uses MediaPipe for skeletal tracking and SSD MobileNet for object recognition to create a unified representation of humanobject interaction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'bounding box coordinates', 'C_o': 'classification confidence of object', 'M': 'movement vector of object'}
primitives.assumptions: Objects are detectable in frame; bounding boxes are stable across frames; object motion is consistent with physical laws.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Object detection fails when classification confidence falls below 0.65 or object is partially occluded.

layer2.mapping: SSD MobileNet's object kernel is integrated into GSE's environmental awareness layer for interaction context.
layer2.telemetry: Pre-trained COCO model fine-tuned on interaction objects

reasoning_traces.think:
ForcePose constructs a unified representation of human-object interaction by fusing MediaPipe's skeletal tracking with SSD MobileNet's object detection. The pose estimation module extracts 2D joint coordinates (P_i) and temporal sequences (T), while object detection provides bounding boxes (B) and movement vectors (M). These features are processed through a custom neural network that learns spatiotemporal patterns linking pose dynamics to force magnitudes (F) and directions (θ). The model's architecture integrates spatial features from pose landmarks and temporal features from motion trajectories, enabling force estimation without physical sensors. The dual nature of this approach lies in its ability to simultaneously decode geometric structure and dynamic behavior from visual input. Failure modes include occlusion, low confidence in pose estimation, and misclassification of objects. The system's robustness depends on filtering mechanisms and normalization techniques that mitigate variability in body size and object scale. This formulation enables real-time inference on standard hardware, aligning with the goal of accessible force analysis in field settings.
